 Why US airstrikes are failing to stop the global cocaine boom
 Juan Forero , The Wall Street Journal 7 min read 14 Oct 2026, 06:37 AM IST 
 Summary
 Smugglers are shifting routes and using new tactics to evade military targeting, resulting in record supplies and plunging prices. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 BUENAVENTURA, Colombia—The Trump administration’s bombing campaign against cocaine-smuggling speedboats is starting to have an impact on the global drug trade—but not necessarily in a good way.
 Thirteen months into the initiative, Colombian navy divers are detecting greater use of “parasites”—metal modules packed with cocaine that traffickers bolt onto the hulls of freighters preparing to steam out of this country’s largest Pacific port.
 Deep in the Amazon, smugglers have shifted shipments east, hiding drugs on boats moving through the rain forest’s vast river network. And on Colombia’s long coast, crews evade U.S. military airstrikes by hugging the shoreline in the exact same speedboats the Americans are targeting.
 Record supplies of cocaine still arrive in the U.S.., Europe and as far away as Australia every day, cheaper and purer than they’ve been in decades, said law-enforcement officials across four continents.
 President Trump has celebrated the airstrikes, noting his administration has “made tremendous strides in stopping the flow of illegal drugs into our country.” In the past 13 months, American military drones and aircraft have destroyed more than 70 vessels, killing nearly 240 crew members and depriving criminal groups of $1.5 billion in cocaine, according to U.S. officials.
 “The drugs coming in by sea are down by 97%,” Trump said in June. “We’re trying to figure out who the 3% are, because they are the bravest people on earth.”
 Yet scholars of the cocaine trade and U.S. officials familiar with the program say drug boats in large numbers still leave Colombia, which produces 70% of the world’s cocaine.
 “The boats keep going. The Pacific is vast,” said Ervyn Norza, a former police investigator who researches the drug trade for Rosario University in Bogotá.
 Felipe Botero, a researcher for the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, a Geneva-based nonprofit, said the American military campaign gives priority to flash-bang visibility over genuine disruption. Traffickers have responded by spreading shipments across cargo containers, freighters, fishing boats, and submarine-like vessels. Guyana and Suriname have emerged as new platforms for cocaine-laden boats, U.S. and European officials say, while Venezuela remains a critical launchpad.
 “This is a policy that’s more about visibility and narrative—showing decisive action—than one that genuinely disrupts organized crime,” Botero said.
 The resulting trafficking network is more diffuse and expansive than before the missile strikes from drones and aircraft began. Colombia is growing more coca leaf and churning out more finished cocaine than at any point in its history, United Nations researchers say.
 Colombia’s new president has vowed to deliver an iron-fisted response, working with U.S. intelligence to neutralize the commanders of drug trafficking groups and pledging to restart fumigation of drug crops, which ended in 2015. He faces long odds: Clandestine labs produce more than 3,300 tons of cocaine annually and armed groups have nearly doubled their ranks to 28,000 members during the past four years, the Ideas for Peace Foundation says.
 The scale of the trade is evident on the streets of drug-consuming countries, where supply is outstripping demand to the point that prices are plunging. In Miami, wholesale cocaine sold for about $16,500 a kilogram this summer, well below the historical $22,000 to $25,000 range. Similarly, European prices have plummeted from $45,000 to as low as $16,000 a kilogram in some cities.
 In both markets, purity remains remarkably high, sometimes hitting 98% in Europe, because dealers no longer need to stretch supplies with adulterants.
 U.S. officials with deep experience fighting the drug trade said the airstrikes cost traffickers money, strike fear into the smuggling supply chain and prevent some shipments from reaching American cities.
 But these officials acknowledge that massive quantities of cocaine continue to flow.
 Ric Curtis, a professor at John Jay College of Criminal Justice who tests drug toxicity at a South Bronx harm-reduction nonprofit, said New York City users have a steady supply of high-quality cocaine. Unlike past decades, the samples he receives are rarely diluted with other drugs or products that appear like cocaine, as was the case in the past.
 “It’s real coke—I’m surprised,” he said. “The price is right. It’s cheap and it’s widely available, I mean, widely,” he said.
 In Europe, the influx is overwhelming authorities. The drugs arrive on container vessels, smaller boats from way stations in Africa, and semi-submersible vessels that cross the Atlantic to rendezvous with ships near Portugal or Spain.
 Laurent Lanier, senior analyst for the European Union Drugs Agency, said the volume is so high that bargain-basement prices are attracting new customers who in the past couldn’t afford cocaine.
 “It’s just crazy the amount of cocaine we get in Europe,” he said.
 France illustrates the difficulty of containing the supply. In 2025, the country seized a record 92 tons of cocaine, a 204% increase from 2022, said the publicly funded French Monitoring Center for Drugs and Drug Addiction.
 Traffickers have shifted from major gateways like Le Havre in Normandy to smaller ports to evade controls, while airliners bring additional supplies smuggled from French Guiana and French islands in the Caribbean. docs.title: Fire and smoke are choking Southeast Asia—but Singapore is equipped to save the day
docs.text:
Opinion 
 Fire and smoke are choking Southeast Asia—but Singapore is equipped to save the day
 David Fickling 4 min read 14 Oct 2026, 03:00 PM IST 
 Summary
 The city-state could use its financial heft to ensure accountability from its less cooperative neighbours. While businesses in the region may prosper from lax regulation, the vast majority of its ordinary citizens are suffering. Not to mention its rainforests. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 A cloud of haze has descended across Southeast Asia over the past few months as a brutal El Niño helps incinerate forest and scrub in Indonesia. The smoke has spread across the region, forcing schools to close in Malaysia, diverting flights and giving tiny Singapore the world’s worst air pollution. If these trends persist, this episode may turn into the worst in Southeast Asia since devastating wildfires in 2015. 
 To hear the way this is talked about in Singapore, the situation is an act of God: Fires just happen and no one can be sure exactly who is responsible. A more sophisticated diagnosis blames intransigence in Indonesia. 
 When Singapore passed a law in 2014 threatening millions of dollars in fines for companies causing haze, Indonesia’s refusal to cooperate made it impossible to implement. For the city-state, discretion towards its giant neighbour has become the better part of diplomacy. 
 It’s hard to discern who is responsible for the region’s forest fires because laws across the region are riddled with loopholes. With officialdom in Indonesia and Singapore blaming each other for the grim state of affairs, smallholders and businesses can get on with despoiling the landscape without accountability. 
 The central problem lies in Indonesia’s fragmented oil palm, timber and paper industries. In each case, large companies control key supply nodes, such as palm oil mills and pulp factories, as well as significant plantation estates. 
 While Malaysia’s plantation companies such as SD Guthrie are mostly based in Kuala Lumpur, many of Indonesia’s largest businesses are listed or headquartered instead in Singapore, the region’s leading capital market and private wealth hub. 
 Beneath these giants is a complicated network of suppliers. In palm oil, that includes millions of smallholders—often poor rural farmers managing just a few hectares, sometimes with uncertain rights to their land and under far less scrutiny from government forestry officials. Their crops frequently pass through intermediaries before reaching mills. 
 Pulpwood, by contrast, comes predominantly from large forestry concessions, whose ownership and relations with the major producers aren’t always transparent. 
 Agribusiness companies source materials both from their own, more closely monitored plantations, and from outside suppliers whose environmental practices can be much harder to establish. 
 The result is a chronic governance gap. Singapore attempted to bring legal action against six companies over the 2015 fires, which cost the economy $1.4 billion and led to 100,000 deaths across the region. But two of the cases were dropped, and in the other four, Jakarta refused to cooperate with Singaporean authorities’ requests to question a director. 
 It is similarly argued that maps that would be needed to establish concession boundaries—and thus link liability with the clear evidence of fire hotspots provided by satellite imagery—cannot be handed over because of Indonesia’s freedom of information laws. Faced with this pushback, Singapore allowed the cases to disappear into limbo. 
 That’s too passive an approach. The four unresolved cases didn’t involve obscure and remote companies, but major suppliers to Asia Pulp & Paper, part of the Sinar Mas business empire controlled by Indonesia’s Widjaja family. Another business associated with the family, Golden Agri-Resources, has long been embedded in Singapore’s corporate establishment. 
 If Singapore were serious about tackling this problem, it would leverage Indonesia’s reliance on its financial sector. Plantation companies seeking listings, loans or capital there should be required to provide up-to-date maps of their concessions and suppliers. 
 Singapore could impose the same principle that the EU applies to palm oil: produce must be traceable to the plots where it was grown, rather than vanishing into a mill where fruit farmed responsibly gets mixed with stuff of murkier provenance. 
 Turning it into a bilateral fight is a convenient excuse precisely because it lets both countries point fingers at each other. The truth, though, is that groups in each of them do well off the broken status quo, to the detriment of the vast majority who must live with the choking, eye-watering consequences—not to mention the rainforest itself, which is more shrunken and degraded with each passing year. 
 The aftermath of Singapore’s 2014 law proved that responsibility for haze can drift and disperse over international borders quite as effectively as the smog itself. If anything good can come out of Southeast Asia’s pollution disaster of 2026, let’s hope it is rules that can finally deliver accountability to those who profit from the burning of a rainforest. ©Bloomberg 
 The author is a Bloomberg Opinion columnist covering climate change and energy .

docs.title: Capital goods stocks fall after multibagger rally. Is this a buying opportunity for long-term investors?
docs.text:
The rally has come at a time when broader markets have been impacted by escalating geopolitical tensions. However, the sector has attracted investor interest amid a widening global supply-demand gap for high-voltage power equipment, including transformers, switchgear, and circuit breakers, as well as strong multi-year order pipelines for companies in both domestic and international markets. However, the rally in these stocks has recently paused as investors appear to be booking profits amid concerns over elevated valuations. Nevertheless, domestic brokerage firm 360 ONE Capital Markets said the recent price correction in these stocks has eased concerns over rich valuations, as much of the potential upside had already been priced in, leaving little room for error. In its latest report, the brokerage has initiated coverage on three companies exposed to the high-voltage power equipment theme: Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and CG Power and Industrial Solutions. The brokerage sees a structural, multi-year growth opportunity in T&D, driven by high-voltage direct current (HVDC) technology, transformers, and grid expansion. However, it believes the companies’ earnings trajectories and exposure to higher-growth adjacent segments differentiate them. Among these, the brokerage believes Hitachi Energy India offers the strongest upside at current valuations, supported by its structural growth drivers and relatively higher exposure to non-T&D opportunities such as data centers, semiconductors, and renewables. The brokerage has assigned a Buy rating to Hitachi Energy India, GE Vernova T&D India, and Siemens Energy India, with target prices of ₹ 36,849, ₹ 4,919, and ₹ 3,101, respectively. These target prices imply upside potential of 10%–20%. It has assigned a Hold rating to CG Power and Industrial Solutions, with a target price of ₹ 886. The brokerage highlighted that renewable energy capacity is projected to rise from 283.5 GW in March 2026 to 596.3 GW by FY32 and 786 GW by FY36, accounting for around 71% of the projected total generation capacity of 1,121 GW. With renewable generation concentrated away from load centers and providing limited inertia, this transition is reshaping grid requirements. Long-distance power evacuation will increasingly require HVDC systems, while grid stability needs are expected to drive demand for static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs), reactors, and other flexible AC transmission systems (FACTS) solutions. Transformation capacity is expected to nearly double from 1,450,526 MVA in March 2026 to 2,411,885 MVA by FY32, underpinning approximately ₹ 9.2 trillion in transmission investments. The brokerage also highlighted that a global shortage of high-voltage equipment is creating export opportunities that were largely absent during the previous cycle. GE Vernova T&D India's export share increased from 17% of revenue in FY20 to 33% in FY26, while Hitachi Energy India's bidding mix implies an export exposure of 29%–30%. CG Power and Industrial Solutions' $99 million Tallgrass Order also marks its entry into the US hyperscale data center market. Importantly, export demand is skewed towards HVDC systems, grid modernization, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS), and instrument transformers, supporting a structurally stronger product mix and pricing. According to the brokerage, data centers provide another growth driver, with India's installed capacity below 2 GW compared with an expected 13–18 GW by 2030. This translates into an estimated ₹ 850 billion– ₹ 1,050 billion opportunity for Hitachi Energy India, equivalent to 1.0–1.5 times its FY26 revenue. docs.title: Adobe, Microsoft… who’s next? AI enabled clones of packaged software have made the industry sit up
docs.text:
Opinion 
 Adobe, Microsoft… who’s next? AI enabled clones of packaged software have made the industry sit up
 Mint Editorial Board 3 min read 15 Oct 2026, 07:30 AM IST 
 Summary
 The latest warning shot is an artificial intelligence-enabled clone of an Adobe suite that took very little time and money compared to the original. Microsoft’s wares are a target too. Software package incumbents need to fortify themselves. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Artificial intelligence (AI) has even begun to disrupt the packaged software industry. Adobe, famous for its design tools, recently received a shot across its bow. Developer Brandon Thomas used an Anthropic AI model and the open-source Rust programming language to build ArtCraft, a free alternative to Adobe’s Creative Cloud suite. 
 The seven-app package, released on GitHub, lacks the original’s finesse, features and more. But it is clear how easily replicas can be made of stuff developed by big companies. In its last fiscal year alone, Adobe invested $4.3 billion in R&D, almost a fifth of its annual revenue. All Thomas needed was a few months with Claude Opus 5.5 to ‘vibe-code’ the apps in Rust. 
 As other developers pitch in to give ArtCraft feature parity, an entire industry stands exposed to such pursuits. 
 Thomas has cloned Microsoft Office too; Autodesk is next. AI coding tools do not need one to copy the target’s source code. Whether such efforts constitute legitimate competition or cross legal limits is a question of detail that jurists may or may not be able to grasp. In the interim, clones could blunt the edge of established vendors and cramp their pricing power. 
 In February, Anthropic’s release of 11 open-source agentic AI tools for its Claude Cowork platform had rattled global software stocks and pushed Indian IT companies on the defensive, as investors asked whether agents could replace software products and services at scale. The same lab’s Mythos model then took the shape of a wrecking ball for cybersecurity sellers. 
 Even software-as-a-service firms are feeling the heat. In a post, Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu said the company would have to reinvent itself amid an “uncertain business outlook for software.” Rising server costs and AI bills have begun to weigh on companies like Zoho. 
 Cheap software scrambled together with AI cannot count on instant adoption, though; at least not by users who need reliable and secure systems. It can take much more effort to review AI-spun code than human work. Running such software locally without telemetry may reduce privacy risks, but does not assure either reliability or security. 
 Corporate users would also be wary of the intellectual property questions that arise. Thomas claimed a “ clean room” approach that used new code based on public specifications and observed behaviour, instead of copying Adobe’s source code. This method does have precedents. However, matters of copyright, trademarks and trade secrets are not treated the same way across jurisdictions. 
 By now, software companies must be well aware that customers may switch to free or cheaper options if the latter find the trade-offs acceptable. Given their deep pockets, incumbents could try buying out startups that pose a threat, although this could invite even more cloning. 
 Open-source offerings could aim for the enterprise market with quality and legal assurances, much as IBM’s Red Hat does for Linux. Software majors could also leverage their brand appeal, distribution networks and client relationships, while upgrading their warranty coverage of risks. With some effort, users who dabble with other options could potentially be lured back. 
 How the market pie of packaged software is eventually shared will be determined by what users trust. In that sense, this contest has only just begun. As with Indian IT services, it also makes space for contrarian bets on this industry’s future.

docs.title: Personal loan closure: How long does it take for your credit score to improve?
docs.text:
Paying the final equated monthly instalment (EMI) on a personal loan does not guarantee an immediate improvement in the borrower’s CIBIL score. The lender must first report the loan closure to the credit bureau, after which the updated information is processed and reflected in the credit report.
Under Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, credit institutions are required to update credit information every fortnight from January 1, 2025. However, the time taken for the revised information to appear in an individual’s credit report can vary.
Moreover, closing a loan is only one of several factors that influence a credit score. According to TransUnion CIBIL, payment history, credit utilisation, the age of credit accounts and recent credit enquiries also affect an individual’s credit profile. Consequently, a borrower may see no immediate change in the score even after repaying a personal loan in full.How long does a credit score update take?
After making the final payment, borrowers should check whether the lender has reported the account as closed and updated the outstanding balance to zero.
Credit bureau updates are not necessarily reflected in the consumer’s report immediately after the payment. According to CIBIL’s consumer guidance, recent payment updates may take around 15 to 30 days to appear, depending on the reporting and processing cycle.
For instance, a borrower who repays a personal loan on October 5 may still see the earlier account status when checking the credit report a few days later.
Borrowers should also distinguish between an account marked as ‘closed’ and one reported as ‘settled’. A fully repaid loan should be reported accurately, in accordance with the repayment arrangement. An incorrect status could affect how lenders assess a future credit application.
Why may the CIBIL score remain unchanged?
A personal loan is an unsecured credit facility. Repaying it reduces the borrower’s outstanding debt, but the resulting effect on the credit score depends on the overall credit profile.
Consider a borrower who has a personal loan, two credit cards and a home loan. Closing the personal loan removes one active credit account, but the utilisation of the credit cards, repayment history and other outstanding obligations continue to influence the credit profile.
The age of credit accounts and recent applications for credit also remain relevant. As a result, one borrower may experience a modest improvement, another may see no immediate movement, while a third may notice a change after updated information is processed.
Should you take another loan to improve your score?
Borrowers should not assume that keeping an active loan is necessary to maintain a healthy credit score. Taking another personal loan solely to improve the score could create an unnecessary repayment obligation and trigger a fresh credit enquiry.
CIBIL recommends paying dues on time, maintaining control over credit utilisation and avoiding multiple credit applications within a short period.
What should borrowers do if the score does not improve?If the score remains unchanged after loan closure, borrowers should first review their credit reports rather than apply for fresh credit.Check the account status, outstanding balance, payment history and date of the latest update. If the loan continues to show an incorrect balance or status after a reasonable reporting period, contact the lender and request a correction.A dispute can also be raised with CIBIL if the information reported is inaccurate. However, the bureau cannot independently alter account information without the required confirmation from the concerned credit institution.Ultimately, closing a personal loan reduces outstanding debt, but a credit score reflects a borrower’s broader credit history. Allow sufficient time for the reporting process, verify that the account has been updated correctly and continue meeting other credit obligations on schedule.

docs.title: How to invest in US stocks from India: Check options to buy shares of American companies like Apple, Tesla and more
docs.text:
RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme ( LRS ) allows resident Indians to send money abroad. The limit is $250,000 per financial year for permitted transactions, including overseas share investments. Open an account with a broker accepting Indian residents. Examples include Interactive Brokers, Vested, and platforms that work with local brokers. Transfer money from your bank through LRS, converting rupees into dollars. Once funds reach your brokerage account, you can buy stocks on major US exchanges. These include the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. You choose which shares to buy, hold or sell. GIFT City in Gujarat offers investment platforms regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority. Platforms such as INDmoney provide access to US stocks through this setup. You still transfer dollars under your LRS limit. Money enters a US stocks wallet and becomes available within 24 hours. NSE International Exchange also offers depository receipts linked to selected US companies. However, these cover roughly 50 stocks, offering fewer choices than overseas brokerage accounts. Indian mutual funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) offer an indirect route. Some invest through international funds, while others follow indices such as the Nasdaq-100 or theS&P 500. You invest in rupees using your demat account or mutual fund app. This avoids international bank transfers and LRS paperwork. However, you cannot choose individual stocks through these funds. Expenses may be higher because fees may apply at both the fund and share levels. Overseas investment limits can also disrupt access. Some fund houses have paused fresh investments when limits approach capacity. GIFT City also offers fund structures that pool money into international assets. These provide broad exposure to the US market under an Indian regulatory framework. Their structures offer different arrangements for individual and institutional investors. Tax collected at source (TCS) applies to certain LRS transfers above ₹ 10 lakh. The rate is 20%, excluding transfers for education or medical needs. You can adjust TCS against your tax bill. US dividends generally incur a 25% withholding tax for individuals under the tax treaty. Submit Form W-8BEN to your broker to claim this rate. Dividends are also taxable in India. Gains on shares held for more than 24 months are subject to a 12.5% tax. Shorter holdings are subject to your income tax slab rate. You must disclose foreign assets and file an income tax return. Sounak has contributed to widely read digital publications. He continues to build a body of journalism shaped by consistency, speed and editorial clarity. He is particularly interested in the intersection of media, popular culture and public conversation in contemporary India.

At LiveMint, he writes daily coverage as well as analytical pieces that interpret numbers, trends and cultural moments in accessible language. His approach prioritises factual depth, balanced framing and reader trust. The reporting aligns with modern newsroom standards of transparency and credibility.

Outside daily reporting, he explores storytelling across formats including podcasts, filmmaking and narrative non-fiction. Through his journalism, Sounak aims to document the rhythms of modern entertainment and sports while maintaining rigorous editorial integrity.

Sounak continues to develop audience-focused journalism that connects speed with substance in a rapidly-changing information environment. docs.title: Starlink suspicions and a frantic warning: Inside Trump’s turn on Zelensky

Global 
 Starlink suspicions and a frantic warning: Inside Trump’s turn on Zelensky
 Robbie Gramer , Lindsay Wise , Marcus Walker , The Wall Street Journal 6 min read 15 Oct 2026, 06:40 AM IST 
 Summary
 Limitations on Ukraine’s access to military-grade Starlink terminals sparked panic among its officials and several U.S. lawmakers. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 In the early hours of Wednesday morning, Denys Sienik, the top Ukrainian diplomat in Washington, D.C., sent a frantic message to U.S. lawmakers: Ukraine was suddenly facing restrictions on its military-grade Starlink terminals, and he didn’t know why. The change, Sienik warned, would give Russia an upper hand in the war and make it tougher for Kyiv to intercept strikes against Ukrainian civilians.
 By the time Washington’s morning rush hour was under way, other Ukrainian officials were already suspecting the worst: that President Trump had ordered Elon Musk, who owns the company that operates Starlink, to throttle Ukraine’s access to the satellite systems.
 The suspicions, which haven’t been confirmed, underscore the extent to which the U.S.-Ukraine relationship has soured in recent weeks as Trump has sought an end to the war.
 In recent days, Trump has offered to buy Moscow’s oil in a lucrative diesel deal, demanded that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky step down, and declared an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine that Moscow almost immediately violated.
 The result: A livid Ukraine, rattled U.S. allies, and a widening rift in the Republican Party over Trump’s foreign policy ahead of the midterm elections.
 “It’s a major problem, and we will do everything we can to fix this,” said Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R., Pa.). Fitzpatrick, who is facing a tight re-election campaign, said Congress would act if it turned out the U.S. government had imposed speed limits on Ukraine’s military-grade Starlink access.
 “If we start going dark on Ukraine there will be consequences, mark my words,” he told The Wall Street Journal.
 Asked what consequences he meant, Fitzpatrick said Congress could hold up funding for any federal agencies that are responsible. “Agencies won’t get funding if they’re not doing their jobs,” he said.
 SpaceX declined to comment on the incident on Wednesday, but Musk noted in a social-media post that limits on Starlink’s military platform Starshield are set by the Pentagon and “ultimately” Trump himself. He didn’t mention Ukraine. “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk wrote.
 The White House declined to answer questions on the Starlink matter. In a statement, the White House said “the President and his team remain committed to continuing to play a constructive role in ending the war between Russia and Ukraine, and he remains optimistic that we’ll ultimately get a peace deal done.”
 Ukraine’s difficulty in accessing the satellite terminals followed U.S. warnings that Trump could cut off intelligence support or military sales to Kyiv, top European and Ukrainian officials said. U.S. officials, however, deny the threats were ever made.
 Ukrainian officials and European allies are now incensed at Trump, senior European officials said, arguing he is going about peace talks all the wrong way. Ramping up pressure on Russia—not Ukraine—is the only way to end the war, they argue, and Russian President Vladimir Putin will only use any economic lifelines from the U.S. to replenish Moscow’s war chest and prolong the fighting.
 Zelensky on Wednesday told British broadcaster Piers Morgan he felt betrayed by Trump’s offer to buy diesel fuel from Russian President Vladimir Putin. “It’s a pity that we are losing a strong partner,” Zelensky said. “We can’t be weak. Otherwise we can’t survive.”
 Administration officials say Trump remains committed to ending the war and is the only person who can parley with both Putin and Zelensky to forge a viable peace deal.
 They said Trump was working first to de-escalate the fighting between Russia and Ukraine, then bring a new offer to Moscow that would grant it access to economic and political benefits if it adheres to a more lasting ceasefire.
 Administration officials also characterized Trump’s offer to buy Russia’s diesel fuel as a way to both lower U.S. gas prices and dangle an economic incentive in front of Putin to bring him back to the negotiating table. They noted that Trump remained open to a future economic relationship between the U.S. and Russia once the war is resolved.
 Some Republican lawmakers have cheered on Trump’s deal with Russia as a reprieve for American consumers squeezed by high energy prices, while others have rebuked it as a misguided freebie for a Russian leader wholly uninterested in peace.
 In addition to Fitzpatrick, other Republicans speaking out against the deal include steadfast Trump allies facing midterm election battles, including Republican Senate candidates Ashley Hinson in Iowa and Mike Rogers in Michigan.
 Regular critics of the president’s policies who are retiring from Congress, such as Sen. Thom Tillis (R., N.C.) and Rep. Don Bacon (R., Neb.), also have spoken out against the diesel deal.
 Officials say the latest tension between Trump and Zelensky started with a meeting in New York.
 Zelensky flew to the U.S. in mid-September for a United nations summit confident that a lot of things were going his way. Ukraine had blunted Russian advances on the battlefield and Zelensky had several positive meetings with Trump under his belt including a chummy North Atlantic Treaty Organization summit in July.
 But at the meeting, Trump pressed Zelensky on why Ukraine was striking Russian oil refineries, people familiar with the matter said. Striking such infrastructure is a crucial part of Ukraine’s strategy to hit Moscow where it hurt

IDBI Bank stake sale price a surprise; no rub-off on PSU stocks: Analysts
 At the bourses, IDBI Bank stock has been an underperformer and has slipped 13.4 per cent year-till-date (YTD) till October 14 as compared to the NSE 500 index that lost 7.8 per cent during this period
 | Image: Bloomberg
 Puneet Wadhwa New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 7:33 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 The stake sale by the government in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd will not have an impact on the stocks of public sector enterprises, especially the public sector banks (PSBs), suggest analysts. The deal price of Rs 81 per share, some said, is far lower than what the markets expected.
 The markets, according to Ambareesh Baliga, expected the sale price between Rs 100 and Rs 110 apiece, which is closer where IDBI Bank quoted pre-West Asia war levels earlier in 2026. The counter is down nearly 22 per cent since then (till October 14).
 “The stock quoted at Rs 116 a piece in February before West Asia war broke out. So to that effect, the Rs 81 per share price is a disappointment for the markets. IDBI Bank stock will adjust to the reality of the deal price soon,” he said. ALSO READ: IDBI employees' forum seeks review of stake sale, flags valuation concerns 
 On Wednesday, IDBI Bank stock closed at Rs 90.39 levels on the NSE, up 9 per cent. It had hit a high of Rs 93.60 before settling a tad lower.

 On Wednesday, October 14, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd for Rs 52,878 crore post market hours. 
 The process will see the government sell 30.48 per cent of its stake in IDBI Bank, while Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will divest 30.24 per cent of its shareholding. This will leave the government and LIC with residual stake 15 per cent and 19 per cent, respectively.
 The transaction, once completed, will be the largest foreign direct investment (FDI) in India’s financial sector.
 At the bourses, meanwhile, IDBI Bank stock has been an underperformer and has slipped 13.4 per cent year-till-date (YTD) till October 14 as compared to the NSE 500 index that lost 7.8 per cent during this period, NSE data shows. ALSO READ: The fall and rise of IDBI Bank: From bad-loan crisis to the Fairfax deal 
 Most PSU stocks have also lost ground. On the BSE, stocks such as Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL), Gujarat Energy, Ircon International, NBCC (India), Indian Railway Finance Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) and Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers have slipped up to 45 per cent YTD as compared to 14 per cent dip in the BSE Sensex.
 PSU banks such as Bank of Baroda (BoB), Canara Bank, UCO Bank, Central Bank of India and State Bank of India (SBI) have slipped up to 19 per cent YTD during this period, ACE Equity data shows. The BSE PSU Bank index has lost 3.3 per cent, data shows.
 While the price comes as a surprise, said G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomics Research, the road ahead for PSU bank stocks is not smooth. Stiff inflation and a possible rise in interest rates, he believes, will continue to dent the financial performance in the months ahead. ALSO READ: Banks may rejig insurance sales as Irdai proposes sharp commission cuts 
 “I do not advocate buying PSU banks at this juncture. Inflation, high bond yields and rising interest rates are likely to play spoilsport as far as PSU bank stocks are concerned. The second and the third quarter of 2026-27 (Q2-FY27 & Q3-FY27) will be a challenging period for these banks as the overall profitability is likely to remain under stress,” Chokkalingam added.

Jio Platforms set to bring India's biggest IPO on Oct 21, seeks ₹30,213 cr
 The fresh issue comprises up to 270 million equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each
 The IPO is set to become India’s largest, with JPL seeking to raise ₹30,213 crore at the upper end of the price band, thus valuing it at about ₹10.3 trillion
 Gulveen Aulakh New Delhi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 12:56 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), the Reliance Industries-controlled digital services company that houses India’s largest telecom operator Reliance Jio, will launch its initial public offering (IPO) next week at a price band of ₹1,065-1,119 a share. 
 The IPO is set to become India’s largest, with JPL seeking to raise ₹30,213 crore at the upper end of the price band, thus valuing it at about ₹10.3 trillion. The fresh issue comprises up to 270 million equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each. Subscription will open on October 21 and close on October 23, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for October 19, according to a statement filed with the BSE on Wednesday. The offering would surpass Hyundai Motor India’s ₹27,800 crore IPO in October 2024, currently India’s largest, if fully subscribed. The transaction comes as global equity fundraising has weakened, while India’s primary market has remained active for a second consecutive year. 
 Jio Platforms has reserved shares worth ₹500 crore for eligible employees and ₹2,500 crore for eligible shareholders, including individuals and Hindu Undivided Families. Eligible employees bidding under the employee reservation portion will receive a discount of ₹54 a share. The lot size is 12 shares, with subsequent bids in multiples of 12. JPL has filed its red herring prospectus with the Registrar of Companies in Gujarat. 
 The listing comes a decade after Reliance Jio’s launch in 2016, when free voice calls and low-cost mobile data upended India’s telecom sector. Over the past decade, it has expanded beyond mobile connectivity into broadband, cloud computing, enterprise services and artificial intelligence.

 The IPO is also expected to mark a new phase for Reliance Jio, which is pursuing plans that include a sovereign low-earth-orbit satellite constellation and AI-native services embedded directly into its network. The company reported revenue of ₹1.47 trillion and profit after tax of about ₹30,000 crore in the financial year ended March 2026.
 Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio, told Business Standard last week that he was confident the offering would become India’s largest IPO, describing it as a major milestone for the company and the beginning of its next phase of growth. “The IPO is just the start of the journey,” he said, adding that Reliance had a strong track record of shareholder value creation and growth. “Of course, the IPO is the biggest step for us as a company.”
 The offering will not include a secondary sale by existing investors, including Meta, Google, KKR, Silver Lake and General Atlantic, which collectively invested about $20 billion in Jio Platforms in 2020. These investors together hold 30.89 per cent of the company, with Meta owning 9.98 per cent and Google 7.73 per cent. Reliance Industries retains a 66.43 per cent stake.
 Jio Platforms plans to use about ₹27,500 crore of the proceeds to prepay borrowings raised by a material subsidiary. Morgan Stanley and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the lead bookrunners, working alongside about a dozen other banks on the transaction.
 For Ambani, the listing is a starting point for a business that has spent a decade expanding access to digital services across India. “We are a 10-year-old company, and we truly believe that the future ahead is a very exciting path,” he had told Business Standard. “From my perspective, the IPO will be a great place for us to start and go on from there.”

docs.title: Motilal Oswal upgrades Jubilant FoodWorks: Can Domino’s and Popeyes drive 47% upside?
docs.text: When a family orders a pizza on a Friday night, it reveals something about the economy. People tend to order food when they feel comfortable spending on things they want rather than only things they need. The domestic brokerage house Motilal Oswal is betting this mood will improve, and it has turned positive on Jubilant Foodworks, the company that operates marquee brands like Domino’s, KFC and Popeyes in India. In its report dated October 13, 2026, the brokerage rated the stock a 'Buy' and set a target price of Rs 625, which it says is about 47% above the current market price. It first moved to this rating in August 2026 in its report on quick service restaurants (QSR), meaning fast-food chains. According to the brokerage report, “risk-reward is attractive” after the recent fall in the share price. Let's take a look at the key details why the brokerage house is bullish on this QSR stock - Pizza sales are picking up The brokerage report noted, “Domino’s Pizza has demonstrated relatively resilient growth, delivering like-for-like (LFL) growth of 6.5% in FY26.” It tracked like-for-like growth, which compares sales at stores open in both periods. That figure rose from 0.2% in the January-March quarter of the FY26 to 4.1% in the July-September quarter of the FY27. ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Management expects 5 to 7% for the full year. Home delivery makes up roughly 76% of sales, and the company is also trying to win back customers who eat in or take food away. Jubilant Food: Can Popeyes, the newcomer deliver The report calls Popeyes, a fried chicken chain, “an incremental growth engine.” Its revenue nearly doubled in the April-June quarter to Rs 70 crore. Its stores now average daily sales of about Rs 96,000, similar to Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC). The chain has grown from 42 stores to 88 in under three years, and management wants 250 stores and Rs 1,000 crore in revenue within three to four years. Spending on advertising and expansion still weighs on profit. Spending slows, focus shifts Jubilant has already built most of the factories and warehouses that supply its stores. Its eight supply centres can serve about 5,000 stores, so the company plans to make existing stores work harder rather than build more infrastructure. Planned capital expenditure is Rs 750 crore to Rs 900 crore this year, much like last year. The brokerage believes this should improve return on capital employed and free cash flow, which is the cash left after running and investing in the business. Jubilant FoodWorks margins: The key factor to watch Profit margins have stayed around 12.5% for three years. Motilal Oswal report cautioned that “FY27 is likely to be a transition year,” as better sales offset rising ingredient costs. It forecasts a margin of 12.6% this year and 13% next year. "Management aims for a ~200bp gain in standalone EBITDA margin pre-Ind AS over FY24-FY28, although margins have remained broadly flat at ~12.5% over FY24-26. FY27 is likely to be a transition year, with productivity gains largely offsetting input cost inflation," Motilal Oswal added. ALSO READWelspun Corp to JSW Steel: Jefferies’ top metal picks for Q2 The brokerage house report further added, "We model EBITDA margin improvement to become more visible in FY28." What investors need to watch The brokerage expects EBITDA and profit after tax to grow at yearly rates of 13%, 15% and 21% from the FY26-28. It values the stock at 15 times expected 2028 enterprise value to EBITDA. Its Rs 625 target values the India business at 27 times and international operations at 15 times that measure. docs.title: Rs 1.86 lakh cr grid push: 2 ‘under-the-radar’ transformer stocks with 40%+ ROCE
docs.text: India’s rising power demand is creating a need for higher investment in transmission infrastructure. Industrial growth, urbanisation, data centres and electric vehicles are increasing electricity consumption. Peak power demand has already touched 270.8 GW and is projected to reach 500 GW and beyond by 2036. To meet this demand, state utilities and private developers are investing in transmission lines, substations, and power evacuation infrastructure. Government programmes such as the Green Energy Corridor, with a ₹1.86 lakh crore outlay for intrastate transmission, are adding to the investment pipeline. India plans to invest around ₹9 lakh crore in power transmission by 2032. As the grid expands, demand for high-voltage transformers, which play a critical role in transmitting electricity, is expected to rise as well. The industry is currently dominated by large and established players such as Hitachi Energy India, CG Power, Siemens Energy India and Transformers and Rectifiers. These companies have diverse business capabilities across the power value chain, from transmission to High Voltage Direct Current. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Alongside these established names, companies such as Atlanta Electricals and Voltamp Transformers bring a more concentrated presence in the transformer market. Likewise, this article covers two lesser-discussed small-cap transformer companies that are also positioning themselves to benefit from this investment cycle. #1 Kanohar Electricals: Moving Up the Voltage Ladder, Targeting Higher Margins Kanohar Electricals (market cap: 8,309 crore) manufactures equipment for power transmission utilities, Indian Railways, and renewable energy infrastructure. Its main product lines include power transformers up to 500 MVA and 400 kV, Scott-connected traction transformers for railways, and shunt reactors. The company operates two production units in Meerut, at Gangol and Rithani, with a combined annual capacity of 19,200 MVA. Capacity utilisation stood at 29.7% in FY25 and 46.0% in FY26, before reaching 36% in Q1FY27. Management expects the existing manufacturing capacity to support operations through FY28. Navigating Seasonal Lulls and Capacity Typically, transformer deliveries are lower in the first quarter, with the majority occurring in H2 and peaking in Q4. This is the reason for the low capacity utilisation in Q1FY27. Transformer manufacturing accounts for about 85% of revenue. Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) projects for substations and transmission lines make up around 15%. The company is focusing more on higher-margin, high-voltage transformers like 400 kV and 765 kV. Products in the 400 kV category accounted for roughly 70% of manufacturing revenue in Q1FY27. Management is also developing the capability to manufacture 765 kV transformers for future extra-high-voltage projects. The 765 kV Shift and a ₹20,000 Crore Railway Opportunity It will take 3 to 4 years to achieve commercial qualification for 765 kV tenders. Further, ongoing railway modernisations, high-speed rail lines and dedicated freight corridors require specialised Scott-connected traction transformers. Traction transformers are used in railway electrification to supply power to electric trains. Management estimates this market represents a potential opportunity of around ₹20,000 crore over the next 5 to 10 years. The company is adding 18,000 MVA of incremental capacity at the Gangol facility. This plant is designed to manufacture 765 kV extra-high-voltage transformers. The new capacity is scheduled to serve demand starting in FY29. For FY27, the management has set a target of ₹950 crore in consolidated revenue. The company expects the EBITDA margin to remain at the same level as in FY26. Growth will primarily be driven by higher manufacturing volumes and a product mix focused on the 400 kV segment. This order book has an execution timeline of 18-24 months, providing strong revenue visibility. Government entities account for 88.4% of the order book, while private sector clients make up 11.6%. This extends the working capital cycle to roughly 120 days. The company aims to maintain its revenue growth (45%) momentum into FY28. At 45% growth on the ₹950 crore expected revenue in FY27, revenue could reach approximately ₹1,350 crore to ₹1,400 crore. At a realisation rate of over ₹6.1 lakh per MVA, the projected volumes support the company’s targeted revenue of approximately ₹1,350-₹1,400 crore. In Q1FY27, the company's revenue from operations rose by 103.5% year-on-year to ₹137.1 crore. EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) increased by 152.2% to ₹38.8 crore, while the margin expanded by 550 bps to 28.3%. Net profit grew by 140% to ₹27.3 crore. The margin expanded due to higher manufacturing volumes and a shift toward higher-margin 400 kV equipment. The historical track record is robust. Over the last three years ending FY26, revenue has grown at 28% CAGR while net profit has grown at 80% CAGR. #2 Indo Tech Transformers: Expanding Capacity to Capture Rising Transformer Demand Indo Tech Transformers (market cap: 3,437 crore) manufactures a broad array of transformer equipment serving power grid infrastructure and industrial sectors. Products include distribution transformers, power and large power transformers, special applications (inverter, converter) and renewable applications. Across its operating history, Indo-Tech has manufactured over 66,000 transformers. docs.title: ICICI Pru AMC: Jefferies sees 28% upside as alternates biz AUM hits Rs 81,000 cr
docs.text: Global investment bank Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation on ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company, and also raised its target price by 4% to Rs 3,760 apiece. This implies an upside of nearly 28% from the stock’s closing price of Rs 2,938.50 apiece on Tuesday. The investment bank has raised its FY27-FY29 estimated earnings per share (EPS) view by 1-2%. Jefferies attributed its rating to lower reliance on marquee funds, 4-10 schemes within top and upper mid-tiers in the last five years, and expansion of alternates business, which is an additional growth lever. Jefferies said ICICI Prudential AMC is the largest active asset manager in India and has grown faster than its peers. This growth was driven by its larger scheme basket and early entry into the portfolio management services segment. ALSO READFrom the US to Kenya: 6 Indian textile stocks expanding despite tariff uncertainty Jefferies on ICICI Pru AMC: AUM growth The investment bank expects the company’s assets under management (AUM) to expand at 17% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26 to FY29. This will be led by mutual fund AUM growing in line and alternates growing faster. “The company has lower exposure to small- and mid-cap funds, lesser concentration of funds, and continues diversifying into PMS/AIFs,” it said, adding that earnings could increase at 14% CAGR as the AMC continues to invest in portfolio management services (PMS) and alternative investment funds (AIF), and newer initiatives like specialised investment funds (SIF). Jefferies on ICICI Pru AMC: Alternates expansion on track The company’s alternates quarterly average AUM reached Rs 81,000 crore, largely equally split across PMS, AIF, and advisory. The advisory quarterly average AUM declined 6.5% sequentially in Q2 FY27 due to FII outflows, but the company has put in place structures to attract fresh flows when FII appetite improves. “The PMS business benefited from higher inflows into small- and mid-cap funds during the quarter. Within AIFs, ICICI AMC already has private credit, real estate and private equity funds, with pre-leased offices being a potential area of opportunity,” Jefferies said. Jefferies on ICICI Pru AMC: Mutual fund AUM ICICI Prudential AMC’s mutual fund quarterly average AUM grew nearly 4% sequentially. The growth was led by liquid, passives, and active equity, Jefferies said. “According to ICICI AMC, while gross flows were stable, redemptions adversely affected net flows. Further, the composition of SIPs was seen shifting toward small- and mid-cap funds,” it added. ALSO READWelspun Corp to JSW Steel: Jefferies’ top metal picks for Q2 ICICI Pru AMC: 2 big growth drivers to watch The global investment bank expects ICICI Prudential AMC to grow significantly in the coming quarters. Mutual funds and the alternates business will drive this growth. Jefferies sees nearly 28% upside on the stock. docs.title: Aditya Birla Capital set for 24% upside? Why Jefferies is bullish amid rising rates
docs.text: The Aditya Birla Capital share price has gained more than 11% in the last six months. Global investment bank Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, which is among its top picks within non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Jefferies has a target price of Rs 475 on the stock, implying a 24% upside from the current price of Rs 382.80. The investment bank cited healthy momentum in unsecured loans, steady growth in secured, lower risk than peers from IRDAI’s proposed commission limits, and a reasonable valuation for its recommendation. Aditya Birla Capital should benefit from rising rates as 70% of its floating-rate assets and 56% of floating liabilities support net interest margin (NIM) expansion, Jefferies said. It expects standalone loans and earnings per share to grow by 26% compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) each over FY26-28 and a rise in share of business or retail loans should lift NIMs. ALSO READElon Musk’s Starlink is at India’s Door. 4 Sectors That Could Feel it First Jefferies on Aditya Birla Cap: NIM improvement The bank expects Aditya Birla Cap’s NIMs to expand by 13 basis points over FY27 and FY28. “Aditya Birla Capital’s margin has dipped 15bps since 4QFY25 despite a 330bps rise in mix of higher-yielding unsecured loans, in contrast to market expectation of NIM expansion on rising unsecured mix. We think yield compression in secured MSME and wholesale loan book (70% of the book) due to lower rates offsets mix gains,” it said. It expects portfolio yields to also improve as banks reprice loans following rate hikes. Jefferies on Aditya Birla Cap: AUM growth, lower fee income risk Jefferies expects the NBFC’s assets under management (AUM) to increase at a 26% CAGR over FY26-28, supported by sustained momentum in unsecured consumer, steady growth in its secured MSME and wholesale loans, and scaling up of its new gold loan portfolio. The company plans to add 1,000 gold loan branches over the next 3 years (200-300 in FY27). “With insurance commissions at only c.3% of total FY27e PBT (FY26), fee income risks due to proposed tighter insurance commission norms should be lower than most peers,” it added. Asset quality in focus Jefferies sees credit cost of 1.06-1.10% over FY27-FY28. The company’s asset quality has been steady across most segments, with gross stage 3 assets easing to 1.3% as of June from 2.2% in June 2025. Jefferies said credit cost has been stable at 1-1.1% in recent quarters. “While growth in unsecured loans has been strong, unsecured AQ trends for the industry stay benign. Secured MSME loans target larger MSMEs that usually have better credit profile. ABCAP's rural exposure is limited, and thus risks to asset quality from weak monsoon are limited,” it added. ALSO READICICI Pru AMC: Jefferies sees 28% upside as alternates biz AUM hits Rs 81,000 cr Aditya Birla Capital: Well placed amid rising rates scenario The company remains Jefferies top picks among NBFCs on stable asset quality and robust AUM growth. Risks from IRDAI’s proposed commission limits also seem lower than peers. Its NIMS are expected to improve amid the interest rate upcycle. docs.title: From the US to Kenya: 6 Indian textile stocks expanding despite tariff uncertainty
docs.text: India's textile exporters are facing another round of uncertainty as trade negotiations between India and the United States have stalled once again. Despite a framework agreement reached in February 2026, the two countries have yet to finalise a trade deal. According to a Reuters report dated 6 October 2026, negotiations have reached a standstill, with uncertainty over future tariffs remaining unresolved. For India's textile industry, the stakes are high. The US is a major export destination for Indian garments and home textiles. Higher tariffs could make Indian products less competitive against suppliers from other countries. This could affect export orders, revenue growth and operating margins. Prolonged uncertainty could also make it harder for companies to plan production and investments. However, not all textile exporters face the same level of risk. Some companies depend heavily on American customers and manufacture primarily in India. Others have expanded their manufacturing operations across Africa, Southeast Asia and the Americas, offering some protection against India-specific tariffs. The key question is whether overseas manufacturing, geographical diversification and pricing power can help these businesses protect their profitability. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now To examine this, we shortlisted six listed textile exporters with substantial exposure to the US market. These companies differ in their business models, manufacturing locations and financial positions. Their ability to withstand tariff pressures could therefore vary significantly. Let's take a closer look at these six textile exporters and assess how well they are positioned to navigate the renewed trade uncertainty. #1 Gokaldas Exports: African Manufacturing Offers a Buffer Against US Tariffs Gokaldas Exports is a leading apparel exporter supplying global fashion brands. According to its FY26 annual report North America contributed 77.9% of FY26 sales, making US tariff uncertainty a significant concern. However, its manufacturing operations in Kenya and Ethiopia provide alternative sourcing options. The annual report further shows the company's African manufacturing presence offers greater flexibility in serving American customers. Its Kenyan operations benefit from preferential US market access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). The company is also seeing increased sourcing interest from American and European buyers. Its expertise in high-value outerwear positions it to compete for additional orders as global brands reassess their sourcing strategies. Capacity Expansion Supports Growth, but Tariff Risks Remain Gokaldas is expanding manufacturing capacity in Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka. Its second Madhya Pradesh unit is expected to approach full utilisation by Q4 FY27. African facilities could also increase production through additional shifts. In FY26, consolidated revenue from operations rose 3.2% YoY to Rs 3,987.6 crore. However, net profit declined 36.8% to Rs 100.1 crore. US trade measures imposed an estimated Rs 97 crore in additional costs. The company has yet to declare Q2 FY27 results. Its August earnings call indicated that orders for the quarter were already secured. However, prolonged tariff uncertainty, rising freight costs and possible changes to African trade benefits could pressure margins despite geographical diversification. According to its FY26 annual report, the US accounted for approximately 59% of FY26 business, making the company particularly exposed to tariff uncertainty. However, its manufacturing facilities in Ohio and Nevada provide some protection against India-specific tariffs. The Nevada pillow facility commenced commercial production in FY26, while Ohio continues to scale operations. Management is targeting $60 million in US pillow revenue in FY27. Geographical Diversification and Modernisation Support Recovery The FY26 annual report also shows that non-US markets accounted for around 41% of business. The company is expanding its presence in the UK and Europe, supported by established retailer relationships and the India-UK trade agreement. Welspun has also approved a Rs 121 crore modernisation project at Anjar to improve manufacturing efficiency. In FY26, consolidated revenue declined 10.9% YoY to Rs 9,399.1 crore, while net profit fell 68% to Rs 204.4 crore. US tariffs affected demand, pricing and shipment volumes. The company has yet to declare Q2 FY27 results. Its August earnings call indicated that flooding at the Vapi facility could disrupt Q2 operations, with recovery expected in subsequent quarters. Despite overseas manufacturing and diversification, Indian towel and bed-linen exports remain vulnerable to prolonged tariff uncertainty. docs.title: Welspun Corp to JSW Steel: Jefferies’ top metal picks for Q2
docs.text: India’s metal and mining companies are expected to post good numbers for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27). Global investment bank Jefferies has chosen Welspun Corp. and JSW Steel as its preferred picks amongst metal stocks for the quarter. Jefferies on Welspun Corp: To benefit from multi-year upcycle The investment bank said Welspun Corp is well positioned to benefit from a multi-year upcycle in oil & gas infrastructure spending in the US and Middle East, which is supported by local manufacturing in both the regions. The company is expected to deliver its sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth, with Q2FY27 EBITDA seen rising 19% year-on-year. Strong order execution in the US will more than offset weakness in India. Welspun Corp’s pipe sales volumes are expected to fall 16% due to continued weakness in India. ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Jefferies on JSW Steel: HRC prices in focus Jefferies remains constructive on JSW Steel, as hot rolled coil (HRC) spot prices in India are currently 9% above their average for the September quarter. It expects further upside if Asian steel spreads mean revert, supporting a stronger earnings outlook. JSW Steel’s consolidated volumes for the quarter are expected to rise 8-10% YoY. The company’s EBITDA per tonne is seen declining 8-9% sequentially, primarily due to higher costs. However, higher volumes should partly offset margin pressure, with consolidated EBITDA seen rising 5% sequentially. Jefferies on other metal players: Hindustan Zinc, Hindalco, Coal India, among others Volumes Volume growth in the sector will be led by Shyam Metalics and Energy, with 21% YoY growth, according to Jefferies. Tata Steel’s volumes are also expected to rise 8-10%, while Coal India reported a 12% increase. Jefferies expect Jindal Stainless’ sales to rise a modest 3% YoY, reflecting production disruptions early in the quarter. It also sees Hindalco’s India aluminium sales to remain flat YoY and Novelis' volumes to grow just 1% YoY. Margins Tata Steel’s standalone EBITDA per tonne is expected to decline 8-9% sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA estimated to rise 9%. Jindal Stainless’ EBITDA is projected to recover 9% sequentially from the production constrained June quarter. Prices Hindustan Zinc’s EBITDA is expected to rise 7% sequentially, mainly due to higher zinc prices and strong growth in silver volumes. Jefferies expects Hindalco’s consolidated EBITDA to fall 17% QoQ but rise 29% YoY, led by a 15% QoQ fall in India aluminum EBITDA per tonne due to lower aluminum prices. It also expects Novelis' adjusted EBITDA per tonne to decline 9% QoQ to $511. ALSO READTata Steel to Jindal Steel: Key stocks poised to gain as domestic steel prices surge up to 24% Jefferies on metals and mining The global investment bank remains positive on the sector as volume growth is expected to drive earnings in Q2FY27. Jefferies prefers Welspun Corp as it sees a huge opportunity from the growing investment in oil and gas infra in the US and Middle East. It prefers JSW Steel because of rising HRC prices. docs.title: Ather to M&M, Hyundai: Nomura names 5 stocks to ride the EV shift in India
docs.text: Automobile companies with a higher exposure to electric vehicles (EVs), competitive EV products, and an established EV technology are better positioned than traditional incumbents with a predominantly ICE-led portfolio, according to Japanese brokerage house, Nomura. The adoption of EVs in India has accelerated after the West Asia crisis. The penetration of EVs has also been supported by improving product options and quality, EV-supportive policies by the government, and an improvement in breakeven points to buy such vehicles, Nomura said. The brokerage said “stock returns over the next few years will likely depend on the EV penetration of OEMs as a key variable.” ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Key stocks to benefit from higher EV adoption As EV penetration across the country increases, Nomura has picked three original equipment manufacturers, Ather Energy, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Hyundai Motor as its preferred stocks. It also expects Tata Motors PV to gain market share in case EV penetration is faster than expected. “Auto suppliers in general should benefit from rising EV penetration given the higher price points and scope to increase content,” Nomura said, adding that it prefers Sona BLW Precision Forgings and Exide Industries within suppliers. EV Penetration in India Nomura said EV penetration in passenger vehicles has risen to 7.9% by September 2026 from 4% in FY26. EV penetration in two-wheelers has increased to 11.6% from 6.5%. “Delhi, Telangana and Odisha lead PV adoption at 21.9%, 21.0% and 17%, respectively, while Odisha, Karnataka and Goa lead 2W EV adoption at 23.0%, 19.3% and 17.5% ,” the brokerage said. It expects that EV penetration within scooters has reached 25% in September, led by states such as Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Rajasthan. “We believe that the underlying data suggests that EV penetration is at an inflection point across segments; LCVs (light commercial vehicles) could also see a marked jump in EV penetration, in our view,” it added. EV two-wheelers: Breakeven period Nomura said the breakeven period to own an EV scooter over an ICE scooter has reduced to around 2.4 years. In fact, a two-wheeler consumer can get nearly full payback on the capital value of an EV vehicle in 8.8 years. This assumes no resale value, which may be additional, it said. For EV cars, the breakeven period over petrol SUVs has dropped to 3 years for compact SUVs, 2.5 years for mid-sized SUVs, and 2 years for large SUVs. “Consequently, EV penetration has risen rapidly at higher price points. BMW India is getting 30% of its bookings from EVs which has led to 2-3 month waiting period.” India’s dependence on oil imports Nomura believes the government’s focus on electrification is likely to continue given the country imports 89% of its crude oil and 50% of its gas. “India has crossed 50% of its cumulative electric power installed capacity, with 29% of power generation from non-fossil fuel sources. Indian government targets to take non-fossil power generation to 50% by 2030,” it said. The brokerage added the carbon footprint of EVs being sold will continue to reduce over time. Since December 2025, petrol, diesel, and CNG prices have risen by 8%, 9%, and 13%, respectively. Nomura expects further price hikes of around Rs 5-7 if crude oil prices sustain at current levels. “Further increase in fuel prices will be incrementally positive for EV adoption, in our view.” ALSO READWelspun Corp to JSW Steel: Jefferies’ top metal picks for Q2 EVs to drive returns in coming years The West Asia crisis amplified India’s reliance on oil and gas imports. With the adoption of EVs rising and more products becoming available with time, original equipment manufacturers with higher exposure to EVs and an established position are likely to benefit more. docs.title: M&M: Why Kotak sees 40% upside despite tractor slowdown and SUV market share concerns
docs.text: When a share price drops for a year, most investors start asking whether something is broken. The brokerage house, Kotak Institutional Equities says that in the case of Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M), it is not. The firm has set a fair value of Rs 4,000 per share, which is about 40% above the current market price, and has kept its 'Buy' rating. According to the brokerage, “Correction offers a compelling entry point.” Let's take a look at what the brokerage house is saying - M&M: Four key concerns for investors The stock has slipped about 10% in three months and around 20% over the past year, even though the company’s earnings estimates were raised during that period. Kotak lists four concerns that weighed on investors. The first is a slowdown in tractor sales. The second is the loss of market share in sport utility vehicles (SUVs), as buyers moved towards hatchbacks and smaller SUVs. The third is competition from new entrants, especially JSW Motors. The fourth is rising raw material costs. ALSO READNot M&M: 2 Mahindra Group stocks yield over 3%. One pays you to wait, one compounds The brokerage believes the market reaction has been disproportionate to the likely impact on earnings. “In our view, these concerns are largely cyclical or reversible,” the report said. The slowdown in tractor demand, for instance, comes amid a weak monsoon and a high base of comparison. Kotak believes these factors explain the near-term weakness better than a fundamental change in demand for farm mechanisation. The brokerage also pointed out that the company's next three years of cash flows contribute only 14% of its value under its discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation method. Can new launches help M&M regain SUV market share? Competition in the SUV market remains a concern for M&M, particularly as demand has shifted towards hatchbacks and smaller SUVs. The entry of new players, including JSW Motors, has also added to concerns. Kotak noted, "perceived competitive intensity from new entrants, notably JSW Motors" Kotak, however, expects upcoming products to support a recovery in market share. According to the brokerage report, launches based on the NU_IQ platform from the first half of calendar year 2027 could help reverse some of the recent losses. The company also has a sizeable product pipeline. Kotak expects 16 new SUV launches and 10 new light commercial vehicle (LCV) launches by FY31. Why does Kotak see room for long-term volume growth? Kotak's valuation analysis suggests that M&M's current share price factors in relatively modest growth. Its reverse DCF analysis indicates an implied volume compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 3% to 3.5% between FY29-FY50. “We believe the long-term runway remains significantly longer,” the brokerage said. It cited low SUV penetration in India, demand for LCVs from last-mile delivery and infrastructure development, and the structural shift towards farm mechanisation as potential growth drivers. ALSO READAther to M&M, Hyundai: Nomura names 5 stocks to ride the EV shift in India Why has Kotak cut earnings estimates but retained Buy? Despite its positive long-term view, Kotak has reduced its standalone earnings per share (EPS) estimates for FY27-29 by 5% to 8%. The brokerage expects tractor volumes to decline over the next four quarters amid the weak monsoon. However, it sees SUV demand remaining steady, with new launches potentially supporting market share gains in 2027. Kotak values M&M at 15.5 times its estimated core earnings per share for FY28 and considers this valuation inexpensive. Its central argument is that near-term pressures may ease while the company's longer-term growth opportunities remain intact. docs.title: 25%+ sales growth: 2 auto ancillary stocks eyeing more revenue from every vehicle
docs.text: You may have noticed how the placement of headlights has changed in modern cars. In many models, the main headlamps now sit just above the bumper, while slimmer LED daytime running lights (DRLs) occupy the space higher up, near the bonnet. This is more than a design change. Signature lighting has become a way for automakers to distinguish premium models, while LED technology is gradually replacing conventional halogen lamps. The result is a rise in the value of lighting fitted to each vehicle, creating an opportunity for suppliers to grow even without a sharp increase in vehicle sales. India’s automotive lighting market is expected to grow from about $1.83 billion in 2026 to $2.44 billion by 2031, according to Mordor Intelligence, implying annual growth of 5.9%. But the bigger opportunity lies in the changing product mix. As cars get more sophisticated lighting systems, suppliers can earn more from each vehicle. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now A Slow-growing Market, a Fast-changing Product Mix Two forces are shaping the automotive lighting opportunity: premiumisation and rising vehicle production. As LEDs replace halogen lamps and automakers adopt more sophisticated lighting systems, the value of lighting fitted to each vehicle increases. This shift in product mix could drive growth even if vehicle production slows. Production growth provides an additional tailwind. India’s automobile industry produced a record 96.9 lakh units in Q1FY27, up 22% YoY, according to figures cited on Uno Minda’s earnings call. The momentum continued into Q2FY27. Maruti reported a 26.4% increase in sales to 6.96 lakh units, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles recorded a 40% YoY jump in domestic sales to 2.01 lakh units. Tighter Safety Standards Regulations are also shifting lighting design and performance. Automobile Research Association of India has been harmonizing the lighting standards. AIS-198 and AIS-199 are harmonized with UN regulations and global standards. These standards are mainly focused on safety and compliance, pushing car manufacturers toward better lighting technology. This provides an opportunity for component manufacturers to add value to lighting systems supplied per vehicle. Lumax Industries and UNO Minda offer the most direct exposure to play this shift. Both are positioned to benefit from the transition to LED lighting and rising demand for premium lighting systems. Neolite ZKW Lightings, another player in the segment, has received SEBI approval for its proposed ₹600 crore IPO, although the IPO dates have not been finalised. Lumax Industries: The Direct Play on LED Adoption LED lighting continues to be one of the key growth drivers for Lumax. The company reported a record consolidated revenue of ₹4,184 crore for FY26, up 23% YoY. LED products accounted for 61% of those sales, versus 58% a year ago. The trend continued in Q1FY27, with revenue growing 32.6% to ₹1,223 crore, with LED products contributing 63% of the total sales. Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) margin remained stable at 9.2% for the period. Lumax Industries: Financial Performance PeriodQ1FY26Q1FY27YoY Change (%)Revenue from Operations (₹ crore)922.51,223.232.6%EBITDA (₹ crore)84.50113.0033.7%EBITDA Margin (%)9.20%9.20%No ChangeNet Profit (₹ crore)36.251.141.2% Source: Company Presentation The Order Book & Content Per Vehicle Potential The order book at the end of Q1FY27 stood at ₹2,500 crore, up from ₹2,200 crore at the end of FY26. The order book breakdown offers a glimpse of where growth could come from next. Nearly 90% of the order book comprises LED-based products. ALSO READOnly 1 public charger for every 235 EVs: 2 stocks taking on India’s EV bottleneck Management expects this shift could help them to grow revenue by 15-20% annually over the next three to five years, targeting more than ₹9,000 crore by FY31. Higher content per vehicle (CPV) and vehicle volumes will be key to achieving this target. Lumax expects its lighting content per passenger vehicle to rise from ₹15,000-20,000 currently to ₹22,000-25,000 over the next four to five years. At the midpoint, that represents an increase of about 34%. Lumax Industries: Order Book Composition Source: Company Presentation The Tooling Catalyst Another factor could influence Lumax’s near-term revenue and margins: tooling. As automakers introduce new models and facelifts, suppliers must develop customised moulds and specialised equipment to manufacture components for those vehicles. Shorter design cycles can therefore create recurring tooling opportunities. Management expects mould sales to rise to ₹250-300 crore in FY27, up from ₹180-185 crore in FY26, with most of the revenue expected in the second half of the financial year. This could provide meaningful lift to the margin. The Margin Question Management is targeting an EBITDA margin of 10.5- 11% in FY27, and more than 13% over the next three to four years. The expected growth in tooling revenue in the second half is one part of the near-term recovery. In the long term, the company is focusing on increasing localisation of electronic components, including printed circuit boards (PCBs) used in automotive lighting, which management expected to add 70- 90 bps to margins. The gap between the current 9.2% margin and the long-term target of more than 13% is substantial. Lumax’s rising LED mix and order book provide a foundation for growth. But the key metric to watch is whether margins begin to improve alongside sales, and whether the improvement persists beyond the timing-related boost from tooling.
