docs.title: Elon Musk’s Starlink is at India’s Door. 4 Sectors That Could Feel it First
docs.text: Elon Musk wants to enter India. India hasn’t said yes. On Wednesday, 7 October 2026, the world’s richest man said ‘certain oligarchs’ were blocking Starlink from India. He named nobody. ‘You can guess who they are,’ he wrote. Source: X (@elonmusk), Wednesday, 7 October 2026 Starlink says it is ready. It has built twenty gateway sites in India. It still needs spectrum, a second round of security clearance, and approval for foreign direct investment (FDI). Spectrum pricing for every satellite operator still needs Cabinet sign-off. But the real story isn't the fight. It's the businesses that already sell internet in India, from space and on the ground. and what happens to them when Starlink switches on. It won't hit them all the same way. Four sectors sit closest to it. Here is how each one works, and where Starlink fits in. 1. Satellite communication services: Starlink sells the same product This sector rents satellite links to banks, ships, airlines, oil fields, mines, and government users who can't get fiber. Most of these links run on satellites about 36,000 kilometers up, so response times are slow. Starlink's satellites fly at 540 to 570 kilometers. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), the space regulator, has approved 4,408 of them for India. The shorter trip means quicker response times, and that is the very thing these customers pay for. The Indian market is small by telecom standards. IMARC Group puts satellite broadband services at US$ 394 million (m) in 2025. ALSO READ5 Stocks Where FIIs Increased Their Stakes in Q2FY27 Nelco, a Tata Power subsidiary, is the listed name with the deepest exposure. In March 2023, about 26% of all small-dish satellite terminals installed in India ran on Nelco’s network. In 2019, it also won a licence to offer internet on planes and ships in India. Its profits were shrinking even before Starlink's launch. Revenue stood at Rs 3.07 billion (bn) in FY26, against Rs 3.13 bn three years earlier. Net profit fell from Rs 240 m to Rs 30 m over two years. The return on capital employed (ROCE) dropped from 23% to 7% over the same two years. Data Source: Nelco annual reports (consolidated), Screener Now the Starlink link. Starlink already sells Nelco's main products abroad. Enterprise links: Starlink markets business plans worldwide. In India, it has not yet published those prices. Planes: By June 2026, Starlink had signed 41 airlines, covering more than 7,000 aircraft under installation or contract. In-flight internet is one of Nelco's growth areas. Phones from space: Starlink has applied to IN-SPACe for a network of nearly 30,000 satellites that can talk straight to phones. A phone-to-satellite venture in which Nelco holds a minority stake targets an early-2028 launch. Three features decide how this plays out. First, 65% to 70% of Nelco's revenue comes from recurring bandwidth fees, on contracts of one to three years. Each renewal gives a customer a chance to compare. Second, Nelco owns no satellites. It leases capacity, and in August 2025 it signed up to sell low-orbit service from Eutelsat OneWeb, a direct Starlink rival. Third, The Economic Times reported in April 2025 that Starlink had held talks with Nelco and state-run Bharat Sanchar Nigam (BSNL). Neither has announced a deal. So, Nelco could meet Starlink as a rival, a partner, or both. 2. Mobile telecom: The fight is only at the rural edge Mobile operators earn from volume: hundreds of millions of users, each paying a small bill. Starlink works the other way. The overlap sits in rural India. In March 2026, rural India had sixty phone connections per 100 people. Urban India had 151. Rural internet subscriptions stood at 48 per 100 people, against 77 for the country. Price limits how far Starlink can push into that gap. The only India prices it ever showed were Rs 8,600 a month, plus Rs 34,000 for the dish. That list appeared on its website in December 2025, and Starlink later called it test data. Data Source: Company results for the June 2026 quarter, Starlink India website. Starlink later called its December 2025 prices test data. Bharti Airtel earned Rs 264 a month per mobile user in the June 2026 quarter. Vodafone Idea earned Rs 195. But Starlink sells home broadband, so the fairer yardstick is Airtel's home broadband user, who pays Rs 523 a month. Even against that, the Starlink test price is 16 times higher. Capacity sets a second limit. In July 2025, IN-SPACe said Starlink's approved network could deliver 600 gigabits per second over India. We did the calculation. Running flat out every second of a month, which no network does, that moves about 194 m gigabytes (GB). At Vodafone Idea's average of 21.7 GB per 4G and 5G user, it covers roughly 9 m users. That is under 1% of India's 1.07 bn broadband connections (107 crore) in March 2026. ALSO READAce Investor Dolly Khanna Adds Stake in This Smallcap Stock Bharti Airtel meets Starlink from both sides. In March 2025, it signed a deal to sell Starlink kits to its customers. Its promoter group's arm, Bharti Space, also owns 17.88% of Eutelsat, whose OneWeb network competes with Starlink. Eutelsat OneWeb holds its Indian licence and waits on the same spectrum. Vodafone Idea meets Starlink only as a possible rival for rural users. Its 4G network covered 87% of India's population in June 2026. Other operators already cover most of the remaining 13%, so satellite's real opening is narrower: villages have no network reaches. Vodafone Idea plans to spend Rs 450 bn on its network till March 2029. Data Source: Vodafone Idea investor presentation, 2026 3. Telecom towers: Satellites can replace a tower or feed one Every mobile signal needs a tower. That makes satellite both a threat and a tool for tower companies. Indus Towers owns 267,611 towers, up 6.3% in a year. Revenue reached Rs 84.3 bn in the June 2026 quarter, with a margin of 53.6% on earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA). Bharti Airte

docs.title: After a 56% jump in 6 months, Anand Rathi sees 30% further upside in this realty stock - Rationale, target price
docs.text:
After a 56% jump in 6 months, Anand Rathi sees 30% further upside in this realty stock - Rationale, target price
 RAYMONDREL 
 New Delhi, Oct. 14 -- A realty stock has seen healthy gains in the recent past, rising as much as 56% in the last six months, yet brokerage firm Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers believes the stock can rise further by 30% from the current levels. 
 The stock is Raymond Realty. Raymond Realty, part of the Raymond Group, is one of India's fastest-growing real estate developers, headquartered in Mumbai. 
 Recently, on 5 October, the company announced that its pre-sales rose by 98% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.902 crore and collections rose 67% YoY to Rs.682 crore in the July-September quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27). 
 For the first half of the financial year, the company's pre-sales jumped by 111% YoY to Rs.1,602 crore and collections climbed 57% YoY to Rs.1,233 crore. 
 The company said there were no new project launches in the September quarter and growth was driven entirely by sustained sales velocity and steady price realisation within the existing "Address by GS" portfolio. 
 The company further said it is accelerating its growth trajectory over the next two quarters with a strong pipeline of MMR (Mumbai Metropolitan Region) launches, representing a cumulative gross development value of over Rs.4,100 crore. 
 Its gross borrowings during the quarter increased by Rs.125 crore, bringing the total to Rs.1,220 crore as of 30 September 2026. 
 According to the company, backed by liquidity of Rs.306 crore, its net debt stood at Rs.914 crore, maintaining a net debt-to-equity ratio well below its board-approved ceiling of 1 time. 
 For FY27, Raymond Realty said it is on track for nearly 20% growth in pre-sales, ROCE of nearly 20%, EBITDA margin of 17-19% and PAT margin of 9-10%. 
 Raymond Realty share price ended 1.31% higher at Rs.678.10 on the BSE on Wednesday, 14 October, snapping its two-day losing streak. 
 Over the last six months, the stock has jumped 56% compared to a 5% decline in the equity benchmark Sensex. Year-to-date, the stock is up 30%, while the Sensex has lost nearly 15%. 
 The realty stock hit a 52-week high of Rs.741.90 on 25 September after hitting a 52-week low of Rs.350 on 16 March this year. 
 Brokerage firm Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers has a "buy" recommendation on the stock with a target price of Rs.879. This implies an almost 30% upside in the stock from its current market price of Rs.678.10. 
 "We initiate coverage with a 'buy' rating with a target price of Rs.879, based on an NAV methodology. The valuation is supported by the value of the identified development portfolio and the longer-term potential of its joint development agreement (JDA)-led development franchise, with the implied 6.6 times FY29E embedded EV/EBITDA," said Anand Rathi. 
 The brokerage firm underscored that Raymond Realty is transitioning into an asset-light MMR platform, with nearly Rs.52,000 crore of development potential across nearly Rs.25,000 crore of owned land in Thane and nearly Rs.27,000 crore across eight JDAs. 
 According to the brokerage firm, the company's ability to selectively secure mature, execution-ready opportunities, enabling faster conversion from signing to launch and scaling across Mumbai without acquiring land, is the key differentiator. 
 "The strategy is already ahead of plan: JDA contribution to bookings rose from 22% in FY25 to 54% in FY26 and 64% in Q1FY27, crossing the company's 50% target a year early. We see Thane as the cash engine and JDA as the growth engine, with annual cash generation of nearly Rs.600- Rs.750 crore from the combined portfolio to fund further expansion," said Anand Rathi. 
 The brokerage firm forecasts bookings and collections to clock nearly 24% and 46% CAGR, respectively, over FY26-29E.

 Motilal Oswal's research report on ICICI Prudential Life Insurance

Cost-to-premium ratio (ex-GST) declined to 18.3% in 1HFY27, reflecting disciplined cost management and readiness to navigate possible regulatory recalibrations. Aptus Value Housing Finance: Choice Institutional Equities initiated coverage with Buy and a target of Rs 330, about 48% above the last close. Share price about Rs 221.85 on 14 Oct 2026, down about 24% in 3 months. Choice cites about 22% AUM growth, strong profitability and an efficient operating model. 52-week range about Rs 194 to Rs 322.
Choice Institutional Equities initiated coverage of Aptus Value Housing Finance with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 330, which implies about 48% upside from the last close of roughly Rs 223 (my calculation from the headline) and about 49% from the Rs 221.85 quote on 14 October 2026. The brokerage cites about 22% AUM growth, strong profitability and an efficient operating model for self-employed borrowers in semi-urban and rural South India. The stock is down about 24% in three months, and gross NPA rose to 1.7% in Q1 FY27 from 1.52%, so the call is a bet on a recovery in sentiment and stable asset quality. Some figures in the reports conflict, including Q1 profit and valuation multiples, and I flag those below.
Aptus Value Housing Finance is a housing finance company that lends mainly to self-employed borrowers in semi-urban and rural areas, with a base in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The stock has fallen sharply, which is why a Buy call with a 48% upside stands out.
This guide explains the Choice call, the numbers behind it, the valuation, the asset quality trend and the risks. Where I calculate a figure myself, I label it.

A margin of 12.5% to 13% is high for a housing lender, and it is the core of the case for Aptus Value Housing Finance. Together with an efficient cost base it supports a high return on assets.

Valuation multiples differ across pages, so treat the P/E range of 11 to 15 times as a range. At either level, Aptus Value Housing Finance trades below the price to book of many growth lenders, but it also carries rising NPA.
The asset quality trend is the main thing to watch. A gross NPA of 1.7% is still low, but the 30+ days past due figure of 6.87% shows early stress that could turn into NPAs.
 Risk: Competition could pressure yields, and NPA trends in small business loans could hurt profit if they worsen.
The Choice target would lift Aptus Value Housing Finance to about 17.6 times FY26 earnings and about 3.1 times book value, which is a clear re-rating from today. That is possible only if the market again pays up for high-margin lenders with steady AUM growth.
If earnings grow at the 20% or so pace of recent years, the same target would look less demanding on FY27 earnings, but I could not find analyst earnings estimates to check this. The Aptus Value Housing Finance case therefore depends on the next results confirming growth.

docs.title: Down 24% in 3 months, Choice sees 48% upside in this housing finance stock, initiates with buy - check target, rationale
docs.text:
The brokerage's positive outlook rests on the lender's growth prospects, technology-led operating model, strong profitability and ability to maintain relatively low credit costs. It expects Aptus to sustain annual growth of around 22% in assets under management (AUM) while delivering return on equity (RoE) above 20%. The report stated, “We initiate coverage on APTUS with a ‘BUY’ recommendation. We value the company at 2.5x FY28E ABV (based on peer-group benchmarking for financial and operational metrics), resulting in target price of INR 330.0 per share," said the brokerage. The housing finance stock has given weak returns to its investors in near term. It has lost 11% in 1 month, 24% in 3 months and 29% in the last 1 year. In the long term as well, the scrip has been in the red, down 32% in the past 5 years. Currently, the stock is almost 31% away from its 52-week high of ₹ 322.45, hit in November 2025. Meanwhile, it had touched its 52-week low of ₹ 193.50 in March 2026. Aptus focuses on self-employed, first-time homebuyers and low- and middle-income customers in semi-urban and rural markets, particularly in southern India. Choice Institutional Equities believes the company operates in a relatively underpenetrated segment as banks reduce their presence in smaller-ticket housing loans. The brokerage said, “APTUS scaled up its AUM by 20% every year since FY18, including COVID-19 period and, we believe, the pace of growth is repeatable. It serves self-employed, first-time home buyers, a segment banks continue to vacate.” The company operates through an in-house branch network, which the brokerage believes supports customer acquisition, loan underwriting and collections. Aptus had 372 branches as of the first quarter of FY27. Choice noted that mature branches generated significantly higher AUM than newer ones, creating scope for productivity gains as the network expands. Another factor supporting the investment case is the company's technology-led operating model. Despite increasing technology expenditure around tenfold since FY21, its operating expenses-to-AUM ratio remained within the 2.6–2.8% range. The brokerage expects this efficiency to continue as the lender scales up. “APTUS earns the highest yield among listed AHFCs yet keeps cost among the lowest. This combination is driven by an in-house, technology-led operating model. Technology spend rose ~10x since FY21, yet opex-to-AUM stood at 2.6–2.8%,” it highlighted. The report also pointed out that Aptus' lending yields and credit discipline. Its loan-to-value ratio of around 40% provides a cushion against potential losses, while in-house collections help manage delinquencies. Credit costs remained at 0.3–0.5% during FY23–FY26, although the brokerage expects some increase in the coming years. Choice acknowledged that the company's net non-performing assets stood at 1.3%, among the higher levels in its peer group. However, it expects asset quality to stabilise with improving collections and the relatively low loan-to-value ratio. On the earnings front, the brokerage expects AUM to increase from ₹ 13,110 crore in FY26 to ₹ 19,540 crore in FY28, implying a compound annual growth rate of 22.1%. Net interest income is projected to rise from ₹ 1,300 crore to ₹ 1,830 crore over the same period. Profit after tax is forecasted to increase from ₹ 1,110 crore in FY26 to ₹ 1,310 crore in FY27 and ₹ 1,550 crore in FY28. The brokerage expects return on assets to remain around 7.8%, while RoE is projected at 20.4% in FY27 and 20.7% in FY28. However, Choice flagged risks including slower branch expansion, higher delinquencies in small-business lending and Karnataka, competitive pressure on lending yields, and lower assignment income. Overall, the brokerage sees Aptus' growth potential and profitability as supportive of a higher valuation, although investors should weigh the identified risks before making investment decisions. docs.title: IMTC Unveils Live Markets, Expanding Buy Side Choice to Execute Fixed Income Trades
docs.text:
Enables investment managers to connect to the trading venues and dealer relationships of their choice within a single portfolio management, order management and execution management platform.
 NEW YORK , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire-PRWeb/ -- IMTC, the fixed income technology platform trusted by buy-side portfolio managers, today announced IMTC Live Markets (ILM), a connectivity solution that lets investment managers determine where and how they execute fixed income trades.
 Through ILM, buy-side firms connect directly to their preferred liquidity venues and dealers. They consume live market data and route trades to leading electronic communication networks (ECNs) as well as their existing bilateral dealer relationships, all within the IMTC platform.
 WHY IT MATTERS
 Institutional investors increasingly seek flexibility in how they source liquidity across the fragmented fixed income marketplace. IMTC Live Markets places clients in control, allowing them to work with the execution venues and dealers that best align with their investment strategies, trading preferences, and client mandates.
 By combining live market access with IMTC's portfolio construction, optimization, compliance, and order management capabilities, investment managers can proactively identify investment opportunities, construct optimized portfolios, and execute trades within a single integrated workflow.
 HOW IT WORKS
 IMTC Live Markets enables firms to consume live pricing and market data from the venues and dealers with which they already have relationships. Portfolio managers and traders can evaluate investment opportunities across multiple sources of liquidity, construct and optimize fixed income portfolios, stage and execute orders, and automatically route transactions through their preferred execution destinations.
 Because execution is fully integrated with IMTC's portfolio management platform, every proposed trade is evaluated against the firm's investment strategy, portfolio objectives, compliance requirements, and client-specific mandates before execution. Once trades are completed, transaction details automatically flow back into the platform to support allocations, post-trade processing, compliance monitoring, reporting, and portfolio reconciliation.
 The result is a seamless front-to-back workflow that connects portfolio construction, optimization, compliance, execution, and post-trade operations while preserving each client's preferred trading relationships and execution model.
 FROM IMTC CHIEF STRATEGY OFFICER PATRICK DUFFNER
 "Fixed income markets are built on relationships and choice. We're not replacing our clients' trading ecosystem; we're making it more connected, more efficient, and more effective. IMTC Live Markets lets our clients reach the liquidity sources that fit their business, from ECNs to their own dealer relationships, while keeping portfolio construction, optimization, compliance, and execution within a single, intelligent workflow."
 Learn more about IMTC's order management solutions here .
 ABOUT IMTC
 IMTC is the fixed income technology leader trusted by portfolio managers, providing end-to-end portfolio and order management, compliance, and reporting on an AI-enhanced platform so firms can trade smarter, move faster, and scale with confidence. For more information, visit www.imtc.com .

docs.title: Buy Jubilant Foodworks Ltd for the Target Rs 625 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
We have recently upgraded JUBI to BUY in our QSR thematic in Aug’26, as we believe the company is best positioned among listed QSR players to benefit from a recovery in discretionary consumption. Domino’s Pizza has demonstrated relatively resilient growth, delivering like-for-like (LFL) growth of 6.5% in FY26. LFL has improved significantly in recent quarters, from 0.2% in 4QFY26 to 2.5% in 1QFY27 and 4.1% in 2QFY27. Moreover, Popeyes is emerging as an incremental growth engine, with 97% revenue growth in 1Q and average daily sales (ADS) close to KFC. Besides, its reinvestment in supply chain in the last two-three years is sufficient for ~5000 store network in India; hence, the company would focus on productivity. It will lead to better capital efficiency and operating leverage, which should support margin in an inflationary scenario. Following the recent stock correction, we believe risk-reward is attractive (at 15x FY28E EV/EBITDA) and maintain our BUY rating with a TP of INR625
 * Domino’s Pizza growth recovery gaining traction: LFL growth improved from 0.2% in 4QFY26 to 2.5% in 1QFY27 and 4.1% in 2QFY27. A favorable base in 2HFY27, consistent delivery growth and a recovery in DITA (Dine-in and takeaways) should support the growth trajectory. The company has guided for LFL of 5-7% in FY27, implying high-single digit LFL in 2HFY27. Delivery now contributes ~76% of sales, supported by strong brand positioning, higher customer engagement and digital initiatives. Management’s renewed focus on DITA through value offers, store upgrades and dedicated teams provides an additional growth lever.
 * Popeyes emerging as the second growth engine: Popeyes revenue grew 97% YoY to INR700m in 1QFY27, with LFL growth of >40% for the third consecutive quarter. The store network increased from 42 in FY24 to 88 in 1QFY27, while ADS reached to INR96k (equal to KFC), with seven cities exceeding INR100k. Management targets 250 stores and INR10b in revenue over the next 3-4 years. While upfront marketing and scale-related costs continue to weigh on overall profitability, improving store productivity and operating leverage should support margin expansion as the business scales up.
 * Menu innovation and digital initiatives to drive frequency and ticket size: Domino’s Pizza is expanding its menu across value, premium, group-sharing and adjacent categories to drive up consumption across occasions and price points. At Domino’s, value offerings support traffic, while products such as Big Big Pizza, Sourdough and Cheese Lava target higher ticket sizes; chicken, beverages and desserts offer opportunities to increase add-on sales. At Popeyes, differentiated chicken products, sauces and flavor-led launches are strengthening brand appeal. The company’s Domino’s Pizza app accounts for ~70% of online orders, enabling targeted offers, customized combos and loyalty-led engagement and reducing dependence on aggregators.
 * Supply-chain capex largely behind; capital allocation shifting toward growth: JUBI has commissioned its Bengaluru food park in Nov’23 and Mumbai food factory in Mar’26. The company now has eight commissaries that can support a network of ~5,000 stores, providing enough capacity for the next few years of expansion. The company guided for capex of INR7.5-9.0b in FY27, broadly similar to FY26, primarily for new Domino’s and Popeyes stores, store upgrades and technology. We believe better store productivity should support RoCE and FCF improvement over the medium term.
 * Margin recovery likely to expand in medium term: Management aims for a ~200bp gain in standalone EBITDA margin pre-Ind AS over FY24-FY28, although margins have remained broadly flat at ~12.5% over FY24-26. FY27 is likely to be a transition year, with productivity gains largely offsetting input cost inflation. We model EBITDA margin improvement to become more visible in FY28, driven by better sales growth, operating leverage and supply-chain efficiencies. We remain conservative and build in flat margins in FY27 at 12.6% and a modest 40bp expansion in FY28 to 13%, leaving scope for upside if operational efficiencies materialize faster than expected.
 * International operations provide earnings and cash-flow support; underlying demand remains weak: DP Eurasia (26% of consol. revenue) reported 28% YoY revenue growth to INR6.7b in 1QFY27. The business has started to pay dividends to JUBI. However, inflation-adjusted negative LFL growth at Domino’s Turkey and continued pressure at COFFY indicate subdued underlying demand. Hyperinflation, accounting and currency movements also create volatility in reported performance, limiting the business as a near-term growth driver.
 * Valuation and view: We expect standalone revenue/EBITDA/PAT to grow at a CAGR of 13%/15%/21% over FY26-28E, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improving to 12.5-13.0%. The stock is trading at an attractive valuation of 15x FY28 EV/EBITDA (pre-IND AS). We maintain our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR625, valuing the India business at 27x and international operations at 15x EV/EBITDA (pre-Ind AS) on Sep’28E.

Capacity expansion and market share gains underpin growth Strong volume momentum; cost pressures remain a monitorable

It commissioned a 0.6mtpa wall putty plant in Rajasthan in 2QFY27, taking its overall white cement and wall putty capacity to 3.65mtpa. It plans to invest INR35-40b in FY27 and INR20- 25b in FY28 toward capacity expansion, maintenance capex, and coal blockrelated investments.
* JKCE delivered robust volume growth of ~15% YoY in FY26, outperforming industry demand growth of ~7-8%. The growth was supported by capacity expansion, timely ramp-up of new plants, and market share gains across key central Indian markets, while maintaining its presence in the North and South. With demand expected to remain supportive, it is targeting doubledigit volume growth in FY27.
* Its opex/t is estimated to increase ~4% YoY/QoQ in 2QFY27, led by higher variable and freight costs. However, it continues to focus on structural cost optimization through higher green power and alternative fuel usage, clinker optimization, and operating leverage. We estimate JKCE’s consolidated revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR at 17%/14%/7% over FY26-28. We anticipate the company’s consolidated volumes to post ~16% CAGR over FY26-28, and OPM at ~15-16% over FY27-28 (vs. ~17% in FY26).
* Given persistently elevated fuel prices, we recently lowered our FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates by ~7%/6%, respectively, in our 2QFY27 quarterly preview. However, any price hikes to pass on the cost pressure in the nearterm pose upside risks to our earnings estimate. We value JKCE at 17x FY28E EV/EBITDA to arrive at our TP of INR5,960. Reiterate BUY.
 JKCE’s aggressive capacity build-out targets 50mtpa by FY30 
* JKCE remains on track with its aggressive capacity expansion plan, targeting grey cement capacity of 40mtpa/50mtpa by FY28/FY30 vs. current capacity of 32.3mtpa. The ongoing 7.0mtpa Northern expansion is progressing as scheduled, comprising a 4.0mtpa clinker/3.0mtpa grinding integrated plant at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and 2.0mtpa split grinding units each at Bikaner, Rajasthan and Punjab, targeted for commissioning in 1HFY28.
* The additional 10.0mtpa grinding capacity addition is under the planning stage. For its medium-term expansions, the company has planned Muddapur line 2, along with 1 or 2 split location grinding units in Maharashtra, to strengthen its market share in the region. Thereafter, the company plans to commission Panna line III, along with 2 split location grinding units. The 3.0mtpa Buxar grinding unit strengthens the company’s access to Bihar and adjoining eastern markets. Further, the acquisition (60% stake) in Saifco (0.42mtpa) expands its reach in the Jammu & Kashmir region.
* The company commissioned a 0.6mtpa wall putty plant in 2QFY27 in Rajasthan, taking the overall white cement and wall putty capacity to 3.65mtpa. It plans to invest INR35-40b in FY27 and INR20-25b in FY28, including expenditure on capacity expansion, sustaining capex, and coal block-related investments. These investments are expected to enhance capacity, secure coal availability at competitive costs, and expand renewable power sourcing, thereby supporting earnings growth.
* JKCE has targeted to reach 40mtpa/50mtpa grey cement capacity by FY28/FY30- 31. The company’s strong execution strategy is estimated to support doubledigit volume growth over the medium term. However, elevated fuel prices are likely to exert near-term cost pressures (estimates a sequential decline in profitability by INR150/t in 2QFY27). Any price hikes to pass on the cost pressure may drive earnings upgrade. We anticipate the company’s consolidated volumes to post ~16% CAGR over FY26-28. We estimate OPM in the range of ~15-16% over FY27-28 due to cost pressure vs. average at ~17% over FY24-26. We estimate its EBITDA/t at INR924/INR990 in FY27/FY28 vs. INR1,017 in FY26.
* We estimate JKCE to generate a cumulative OCF of INR50.1b during FY27-28, with cumulative capex estimated at INR62.0b over the same period. Given the heavy capex cycle, its net debt is estimated to surge to INR81.9b by FY28 vs. INR55.7b in FY26. The company’s net debt-to-EBITDA ratio is estimated to increase to 2.6x by FY28 vs. 2.3x in FY26. We anticipate its RoE/RoCE (post tax) to remain largely stable at ~14%/10% by FY28.
* At CMP, the stock is currently trading at 17x/15x FY27/FY28E EV/EBITDA. We value JKCE at 17x FY28E EV/EBITDA to arrive at our TP of INR5,960. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock

docs.title: Buy Aditya Infotech Ltd for the Target Rs 5,390 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Scale, R&D and supply chain: Lead widening, runway extending 
Aditya Infotech (AIL) holds ~43.3% market share in India's structurally underpenetrated surveillance market. The ongoing supply chain challenges have further crippled the competition, which has placed CP PLUS in a strong position to gain further share. Incrementally, AIL is strategically expanding its current TAM by adding new adjacent products and exploring expansion in overseas markets. Consequently, the company should continue to deliver a robust performance in the coming years.
* Supply-chain resilience is becoming a competitive advantage for AIL. Supply of critical components (SoCs, image sensors and memory) remains tight. CP PLUS has an edge here due to a diversified base of non-Chinese SoCs and sensor suppliers (Qualcomm, Ambarella, Augentix, Innofusion, Realtek SOC, Sony and others), ~10-15x the scale of domestic peers, with a balance sheet that can carry inventory (unlike peers).
* The company is working on several new growth levers beyond the core business. Recently, the company mentioned about the new product categories (machine vision, industrial AMRs (Autonomous Mobile Robots), smart home security, i.e., smart locks, video doorbells, door phones) and drone cameras, which are under various stages of development. These products can add over ~USD1b of addressable market today, growing at mid-to-high teens. AIL is also actively looking at expanding into international markets, which will open up a huge growth potential for the company and enable it to sustain the high growth trajectory.
* Tech advancement is further strengthening AIL’s market positioning. The company is shifting from being a hardware assembler to a technology-led solution platform. AIL has R&D centers in Noida, Ahmedabad and Taiwan, and is now expanding in Bengaluru, developing new-age & AI-enabled products. Partnerships with Qualcomm and L&T Semiconductor add AI, embedded-software and silicon capability. AIL is way ahead of its peers in domestic markets and is now competing with global leaders in terms of quality and product efficiency.
* AIL's competitive moat is therefore increasingly led by the ecosystem, combining product breadth, manufacturing scale, distribution reach and technology capabilities to create a full-spectrum surveillance platform rather than a single-product security business.
* We estimate revenue/EBITDA/PAT CAGR of 37%/47%/50% over FY26-29. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR4,850.
 Structural growth and a widening addressable market support stable growth 
* India’s surveillance market remains underpenetrated, driven by urbanization, infrastructure spending, IP migration, AI adoption and replacement demand. Higher STQC barriers favor scaled players. CP PLUS holds ~43.3%+ share and is positioned for further gains amid limited peer capacity additions.
* The industry is moving toward IP (Internet Protocol), AI, VMS (Video Management System), storage and integrated solutions, and with CPPLUS’s product offerings (IPs constituting 73% of company’s product-mix), AIL is well positioned to benefit from this structural shift in industry.
* CP PLUS is also expanding into adjacent security and smart-device categories (machine vision, industrial AMRs, smart home security, i.e., smart locks, video doorbells, door phones) and drone cameras, leveraging its existing brand, distribution, integrator network and imaging/AI capabilities. These new categories will expand the company’s TAM substantially (est. from current ~USD2b to USD3-3.5b+).
* Incrementally, AIL focuses on expanding its presence beyond the domestic market. With improving product quality, a strengthening brand image and robust manufacturing capabilities, the company is well positioned to tap export opportunities. A successful scale-up in international markets could emerge as an additional growth lever, diversifying its revenue base and expanding its addressable market.
* Alongside calibrated capacity additions to support incremental growth, AIL continues to step up investments in R&D and technological capabilities, with a focus on developing next-generation, AI-enabled surveillance products to address evolving industry requirements. Further, AIL’s scale and established supply-chain ecosystem provide a meaningful competitive advantage, particularly amid persistent availability challenges for critical components, which continue to constrain the operating performance and growth capabilities of smaller peers. This, in our view, should further strengthen AIL’s competitive positioning within the industry.
* We estimate AIL to deliver a revenue CAGR of 37% over FY26-29E, and with multiple margin levers, its EBITDA margin is likely to expand to 16.6% by FY29E from 13.4% in FY26. Owing to this, we expect EBITDA/PAT to grow 47%/51% over FY26-29.
* We value the company at a P/E of 50x on FY29E EPS to arrive at a TP of INR5,390. Reiterate our BUY rating.

docs.text:
Emkay Global Financial Services named Shree Cement a tactical Buy in its October 14, 2026 cement-sector update, while Shree Cement stock was trading at INR 22,195.00 on the National Stock Exchange at 10:40 a.m. IST. The combination puts the next earnings report at the center of the short-term discussion.
 Emkay favors Shree Cement
 According to Emkay Global Financial Services in its October 14, 2026 update, Shree Cement and Ambuja Cements were tactical Buy ideas. The note also pointed to a possible INR 10-15 per bag cement price increase from October 12, 2026, alongside pressure from higher fuel costs.
 The analyst view is balanced by the latest operating picture. Shree Cement reported revenue from operations of INR 6,233 crore in the first quarter of fiscal 2026-27, up 18.00 percent year over year, while net profit fell 17.50 percent to INR 531.10 crore, according to AlfaFinder . Revenue growth therefore came with a weaker profit comparison.
 What will Q2 results show?
 Shree Cement's board is scheduled to meet on October 23, 2026 to consider unaudited second-quarter and first-half results, according to AlfaFinder . For investors, the key comparison will be whether pricing and volume growth can offset fuel and raw-material costs after the first-quarter profit decline.
 Three dated developments
 Shree Cement's first-quarter fiscal 2026-27 report covered the period ended June 30, 2026 and showed revenue of INR 6,233 crore. On October 8, 2026, Riya Puja Jain requested reclassification from the promoter group to the public category while holding 2,050 shares, according to TapeTide . The October 23, 2026 board meeting is the next dated company event.
 Trading level and key dates
 Shree Cement was at INR 22,195.00 on NSE on October 14, 2026 at 10:40 a.m. IST, with a market capitalization of INR 800.8 billion and a 52-week range of INR 21,355.00 to INR 30,285.00. The figures place the stock 26.71 percent below its 52-week high, calculated from the same currency values.
 Shree Cement Limited is one of India's major cement producers, with installed cement capacity of 69.30 million metric tons per year, according to the company's investor information . Its investor page reports fiscal 2025-26 revenue of INR 19,310.52 crore and net profit of INR 1,706.25 crore.

docs.title: Buy ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Ltd for the Target Rs 540 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Product mix shift drives 100bp YoY margin expansion 
* ICICI Prudential Life Insurance (IPRU) reported APE of INR28b (in line), reflecting growth of 16% YoY. For 1HFY27, APE grew 15% YoY, supported by strong 40% YoY growth in the protection business.
* VNB margin for the quarter stood at 25.4% vs our estimate of 25.5% and 24.5% in 2QFY26. For 1HFY27, VNB grew 22% YoY and VNB margin expanded 150bp YoY to 26%, backed by the product mix shift.
* For 2QFY27, IPRU’s shareholder PAT grew 27% YoY to INR3.7b. EV at the end of 1HFY27 was at INR566.7b, growing 12% YoY.
* Cost-to-premium ratio (ex-GST) declined to 18.3% in 1HFY27, reflecting disciplined cost management and readiness to navigate possible regulatory recalibrations.
* We have maintained our estimates following the 2QFY27 performance, with operating RoEV projected at 12-13%. Key monitorables include regulatory implementations across distribution, IFRS, and risk-based solvency, as well as the impact of a rising interest rate environment. We reiterate our BUY rating with a revised TP of INR540 (based on 1.2x FY28E EV).
 Protection contribution at over 20% of APE 
* IPRU’s gross premium grew 16% YoY to INR142.5b (in line) in 2QFY27, driven by 6% YoY growth in renewal premium, while single premium grew 39% YoY.
* APE growth of 16% YoY in 2QFY27 was driven by 34% growth in protection and 52% growth in the lumpy group savings business, while ULIP grew 7% YoY and non-linked savings grew 11% YoY. Within non-linked savings, contribution of non-par improved to 40%, while par contributed 60%. The rising interest rate environment can likely be favorable for non-par and
* Within the protection segment, the retail business witnessed 36% YoY growth, with its contribution to APE rising to 8.3% in 2QFY27 from 7.0% in 2QFY26. Credit life growth was largely aligned with overall protection growth, supported by a diversified partner network as well as the parent bank.
* Savings business contribution declined to 80.0% in 2QFY27 from 82.7% in 2QFY26, largely owing to the impact of weak equity markets on ULIPs.
* The 100bp YoY expansion in VNB margin to 25.4% in 2QFY27 was a result of a favorable product mix, especially higher protection contribution.
* Commission expenses grew 8% YoY to INR13.8b, while operating expenses grew 45% YoY, resulting in a rise in EoM ratio to 18.6% from 17.5% in 2QFY26. However, cost/total premium, excluding GST, improved 30bp YoY to 18.3% in 1HFY27, while for savings, the ratio improved 90bp to 11.6%, reflecting disciplined cost management.
* On the distribution front, agency (grew 6% YoY)/direct channels (grew 9% YoY) together contributed ~46.5% of retail APE. IPRU is investing in enhancing its tech and analytics capabilities to improve agent productivity, while also adopting a micro-market approach.
* Bancassurance APE grew 4% YoY, contributing 27.5% of APE, with growth coming largely from non-ICICI banks, while ICICI bank has been stable.
* Partnership distribution APE increased 38% YoY, contributing 15% of APE, supported by deeper engagement with existing partners and new relationships.
* On a premium basis, persistency improved in 2QFY27, with 13th month persistency at 83.9% (81.4% in 2QFY26). The 61st month persistency improved to 62.3% (59.5% in 2QFY26) and the 37th month persistency declined to 72.9% in 2QFY27 from 74.4% in 2QFY26.
* AUM grew 2% YoY to INR3.3t, while solvency improved to 229.9% (213.2% in 2QFY26).
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* The proposed commission cuts are likely to have a substantial impact on credit life insurance. However, the regulator is expected to consider the product’s importance, given the large number of lives covered.
* Opex (ex-GST) has declined at an 8% CAGR over the past three years, positioning IPRU to navigate distribution-related regulatory recalibrations.
* The company has repriced non-par products in line with prevailing yields, with competitive IRRs potentially attracting younger customers. Sustained higher interest rates could increase the contribution of non-par and annuity products.
* IPRU’s continued efforts toward the product mix shift and increasing retail protection contribution have resulted in continued YoY expansion in VNB margin. In the long term, the company’s profitability will be supported by sustainable growth momentum and increased traction of non-linked products.
* We have maintained our estimates following the 2QFY27 performance, with operating RoEV projected at 12-13%. Key monitorables include regulatory implementations across distribution, IFRS, and risk-based solvency, as well as the impact of the rising interest rate environment. We reiterate our BUY rating with a revised TP of INR540 (based on 1.2x FY28E EV)
